goldens.comment: OptimizedCursorPaginator's negative-offset branch in get_result() passes cursor.offset directly as start_offset to queryset slicing when enable_advanced_features is True and cursor.offset < 0.
In BasePaginator.get_result(), when cursor.is_prev is True, it sets start_offset = offset without clamping, allowing negative offset values to be passed to queryset slicing.
OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key uses floor/ceil on a datetime key (order_by='-datetime'), causing TypeError.
Accessing .has_global_access on organization_context.member can raise an AttributeError when organization_context is None, particularly for non-superuser non-member users.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/data] src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:197 — Switching from SADD to ZADD without changing Redis key names causes WRONGTYPE errors for existing set buffers and prevents ZSCAN from flushing them; version the keys or migrate the data.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows Redis operations changing from set commands (SADD, SCARD, SSCAN, SUNIONSTORE) to sorted set commands (ZADD, ZCARD, ZSCAN, ZUNIONSTORE) in both buffer.py and add-buffer.lua. The key format remains the same (e.g., 'span-buf:s:{project_and_trace}:parent_span_id'). If there are existing Redis keys created with SADD (sets), attempting to use ZADD/ZCARD/ZSCAN (sorted set operations) on them will cause WRONGTYPE errors because Redis enforces strict type checking. This is a real deployment issue - existing data in Redis will be incompatible with the new code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/data] src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:48 — ZUNIONSTORE sums scores for replayed spans present in both buffers, inflating their timestamps and retaining them ahead of newer spans during eviction; use AGGREGATE MAX.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows ZUNIONSTORE being used at lines 48 and 53 in add-buffer.lua without specifying an AGGREGATE option. By default, Redis ZUNIONSTORE uses SUM to combine scores when the same member exists in multiple sets. Since the scores represent end_timestamp_precise (as shown in buffer.py line 196-198 where zadd uses span.end_timestamp_precise as the score), if a span appears in both sets being merged, its timestamp score would be summed/doubled. This would cause those spans to have artificially inflated scores, affecting the zpopmin eviction at line 58 which removes spans with the lowest scores. Using AGGREGATE MAX would preserve the correct timestamp semantics.
